belay.1: Bolted anchor at the foot of a large ramp, at the end of the face climbing.
belay.2: A stance below the splitter crack, reached by thin aid.
belay.3: A sheltered, slabby station at the top of the splitter cracks.
belay.4: A stance below the mud-filled corner, above the roof and hook section.
belay.5: Belay just below a slab, at the end of the left-facing corner.
belay.11: A grassy ledge reached by easy free climbing.
belay.12: A ledge at the top of the aid through the roof; it also works for a portaledge.
belay.13: A ledge beside the crest of the buttress, at the end of the free climbing.

belay.1: Two-bolt anchor at the top of the slabby left-facing corner.
belay.2: Two-bolt anchor at the top of the thin crack moves above the roof and slab.
belay.3: Two-bolt anchor on the large ledge; the next pitch starts at a cairn along it to the left.
belay.4: Two-bolt anchor just around the arete to the right.
belay.5: Two-bolt anchor on the right side inside the big cave.
belay.6: Two-bolt anchor on a stance beneath the leaning roof.
belay.7: Two-bolt anchor at the left end of the roof, past the pin.
belay.8: Two-bolt anchor on the sloping slab reached by the leftward hand-traverse; ignore the other anchor up and right.
belay.9: Two-bolt anchor at the top of the easy ramp, at the base of the Tiger Flake.
belay.10: Two-bolt anchor on a big ledge at the top of the flake pitch.
belay.11: Belay from a tree near the ridge, above the final bulge.

belay.1: A tree on the ridge crest, left of where the gully tops out.
belay.3: A tree on the large ledge reached by turning left.
belay.4: At the foot of a chimney, on the small ledge system.
belay.5: A ledge just above the big chockstone.
belay.6: A tree up and to the left, or gear above the blocks.
belay.7: A small notch with trees below it, directly under the crux pitch.
belay.8: A tree at the top of the crux, where the pitch exits into the sandy gully.
belay.9: At the base of a corner on the left, above the loose gully and short face.

belay.1: Gear in a horizontal crack on a ledge to the right, above the two small roofs.
belay.2: The large treed ledge at the start of the headwall, using tree or gear.
belay.3: Bolted anchor on a small stance above the finger crack.
belay.4: Bolted anchor next to a dead tree on a flat ledge.
belay.5: Bolted anchor on a stance at the top of the flared cracks.
belay.6: Bolted anchor on a ledge around the corner to the left, above the dihedral.
belay.7: The large ledge with a tree and a cave; use the tree, gear, or pinches inside the cave.
belay.8: On top of the ridge, above the keyhole.

belay.1: Gear anchor in a crack at the top of the corner, after a full rope length.
belay.2: Gear on a small plateau, using small cams or nuts.
belay.3: A ledge above the short gully, using cams in the 1 to 2 inch range.
belay.4: On the ridge crest reached by bearing left from the previous station.
belay.6: At the top of the ridge, with a sling over a rock or a gear anchor.
belay.7: In a notch at the top of the slab beside the wide crack.
